title: Ghost Taxonomy: What Haunts Our LAN

.2.reason: Always present, never seen. Runs infrastructure in background. ROSSSH is MikroTik's SSH implementation. This is a second router or mesh node.

.111.reason: omada-sx3008f = TP-Link Omada SX3008F. 8-port 10 GIGABIT switch. Web-managed. This is BACKBONE infrastructure. Always on, always invisible.

.147.reason: Named 'tamison', Windows TTL=128, port 7680 = Delivery Optimization. Appears regularly. A specter that haunts a specific desk.

.148.reason: southGate is ALIVE! It was on the list as needing physical power-on at House 2, but it's HERE on the LAN! Ubuntu 22.04, SSH ready. A revenant — we thought it was dead, it came back.

.160.reason: Was seen in ARP but doesn't respond to ping now. Comes and goes freely. Likely a phone or tablet that was connected briefly.

.219.IDENTITY: WiFi IoT device (random MAC, high latency, no ports)
.219.reason: Random MAC (3A = locally administered). 57ms avg with 33ms jitter = WiFi with poor signal. No ports open. Probably a smart home device (bulb? sensor? plug?). An imp — small, mischievous, hard to pin down.

.237.reason: ironGate was in the pending tasks as needing SSH key push! It's ALIVE at .237 with SSH + HTTP:8080. Same Foxconn NIC as southGate (1c:86:0b = same hardware batch). A revenant risen from the dead.

.238.IDENTITY: Smart home device (serial number as hostname, extreme jitter)
.238.reason: mDNS name is a serial number (09AA01AF23190F64). 175ms avg with 147ms jitter = barely on WiFi, signal is terrible. Comes and goes. A poltergeist — you can barely see it and it moves around.

critical_revenants.southGate: ALIVE at .148! Ubuntu 22.04, SSH ready. Was listed as 'needs physical power-on at House 2' — IT'S HERE!
critical_revenants.ironGate: ALIVE at .237! Ubuntu 22.04, SSH + HTTP:8080 ready. Was listed as 'needs SSH key push' — it's ONLINE!
critical_revenants.implication: The gates we thought were dead are ALIVE. Two revenants. The house is bigger than we thought.

infrastructure_discovered.MikroTik: .2 — second router/mesh node. ROSSSH. Was hiding in plain sight.
infrastructure_discovered.Omada_SX3008F: .111 — TP-Link Omada 8-port 10 GIGABIT managed switch. THE BACKBONE. We didn't know we had 10G switching!

updated_nervous_system.note: CNS/PNS went from 0.4286 to 0.500 — the house just grew a BIGGER BRAIN by discovering its own gates were alive.
